records.description: Nokia Foundation Fellow grants support innovative and pioneering research projects in Information and Communications Technologies, with the purpose of financing innovative ideas, discovering new research streams and exploring research gaps around ICT. The grant amount is EUR 75,000 and its purpose is to finance hiring a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher to work on the project. Grants are available for projects carried out in Finnish universities, and successful projects may reapply for an extension through the following year's application process.

eligibility: The grant application is submitted and the project is led by a tenured associate or full professor acting as Principal Investigator for their own project
The project is carried out at a Finnish university
Each professor may submit one application per call
The project must be innovative and pioneering research in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT)
The proposal should have the potential to open genuinely new frontiers
Ethical and research security aspects of the research should be comprehensively explained in the application form
benefits: The purpose of the grant is to finance hiring a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher to work on the project
For successful projects it is possible to reapply for an extension via the next year's application process
selection_criteria: Exceptional proposals that have the potential to open genuinely new frontiers
Clear highlight of the innovativeness and the high-risk high-reward nature of the proposed project
Comprehensive explanation of ethical and research security aspects
A detailed financial plan breaking the grant down across the researcher's salary, overhead costs and possible other expenses
application_process: Submit the application through the Nokia Foundation electronic grant application system at nokiafoundation.apurahat.net
A partially completed application may be saved as a draft and continued later
At the application stage it is not necessary to specify which researcher will be hired, but if already identified it is beneficial to include their information
Submit a detailed financial plan showing the use of the grant across the researcher's salary, overhead costs and possible other expenses
official.duration: Granted research projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028
key_dates: Call for applications open from 18 May 2026 to 15 September 2026
Grant decisions scheduled for late October 2026
Successful projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028

applicant_utility.description: This grant is aimed at professors, not students, so its usefulness to most applicants is indirect: it is the route through which a Finnish professor hires a doctoral or postdoctoral researcher onto a new ICT direction, and the EUR 75,000 is explicitly earmarked for that salary. If you are a PhD or postdoc looking for a position, the practical move is to find a professor who is applying and ask to be named in their application - the Foundation says naming a candidate is beneficial but not required at the application stage. There is no template and no page limit, which sounds liberating but actually means your proposal is judged purely on quality and persuasiveness.
eligibility_tips: The applicant must be a tenured associate or full professor applying as Principal Investigator for their own project. Doctoral and postdoctoral researchers cannot apply directly.
The project must be carried out at a Finnish university, which fixes the host institution to Finland.
One application per professor per call, so a professor cannot hedge across multiple ideas in the same round.
application_tips: Lead with the high-risk, high-reward framing. The Foundation asks applicants to clearly highlight the innovativeness and the high-risk high-reward nature of the project, and says it focuses on exceptional proposals that open genuinely new frontiers.
Budget the full EUR 75,000 explicitly against salary, overheads and other expenses. A vague financial plan weakens an otherwise strong proposal.
Treat ethics and research security as a scored component rather than boilerplate - the Foundation requires these to be comprehensively explained in the form.
Use the draft-and-return function to build the application over several weeks rather than submitting a first attempt.
documents: Project plan: there is no template and no length restriction, so the burden is on the applicant to be clear and realistic without padding.
Financial plan showing salary, overheads and other expenses against the EUR 75,000 total.
Ethics and research security explanation inside the application form.
mistakes_to_avoid: Writing a safe, incremental proposal. The Foundation is explicit that it wants genuinely new frontiers and high-risk high-reward work, so a low-risk project is structurally a poor fit.
Leaving overheads out of the financial plan. The Foundation requires a detailed breakdown including overhead costs.
Positioning it as student funding. It is a research project grant that pays for a hired researcher, not personal financial support.
Missing the extension opportunity. Successful projects can reapply for an extension via the next year's process, which is a second bite at funding for the same direction.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: The 2026 window ran 18 May to 15 September 2026 and has closed, with decisions scheduled for late October 2026. The call recurs annually, so watch the page from around May. Note the project clock: successful projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028, a fixed horizon that constrains what kind of research can realistically be proposed.

records.description: The Jorma Ollila Grants fund research visits to host organisations abroad for researchers at Finnish universities. The page publishes the archive of awarded grants, which shows the actual amounts distributed: in 2025 grants of EUR 20,000, EUR 25,000 and EUR 9,500 to researchers at the University of Oulu, the University of Helsinki and Tampere University, with hosts including the University of California San Diego, EPFL and Radboud University. Award amounts vary substantially by visit, with larger multi-year awards such as EUR 50,000 for a two-year visit recorded in 2024.

official.program_type: Research visit grant for researchers based at Finnish universities
eligibility: The published award archive shows recipients based at Finnish universities, including the University of Oulu, the University of Helsinki, Tampere University, Aalto University, the University of Turku, the University of Jyväskylä and the University of Vaasa
Awards are made in support of a research visit to a named host organisation abroad
Topics in the published archive concentrate on ICT, wireless and network technologies, machine learning and data science

applicant_utility.description: What the official page actually gives you is the money, not the rules: the Jorma Ollila Grants page is an award archive, so the most reliable signal available is the range of amounts awarded. Recent single-year visits landed between roughly EUR 9,500 and EUR 25,000, with a EUR 50,000 award for a two-year visit, so a realistic ask for a one-year placement sits in the low tens of thousands rather than the hundreds. Because the criteria, deadlines and permitted costs are not published on this page, treat every figure here as an observed award rather than a promise, and use the Foundation's grant system and general pages to confirm current terms before applying.
eligibility_tips: Recipients are consistently based at Finnish universities - Oulu, Helsinki, Tampere, Aalto, Turku, Jyväskylä and Vaasa all appear - so a Finnish institutional affiliation is the visible pattern in the awardee list.

Awarded projects are ICT-centred: sparse channel estimation, AI alignment, neural network interpretation, 6G RF transmitters, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces and digital healthcare all feature, which gives a clear sense of the thematic centre of gravity.
A named host institution abroad is a feature of every award, so a concrete invitation appears to be part of a credible application.
application_tips: Use the archive to calibrate your budget request rather than inventing a number: single-year awards cluster in the EUR 9,500-25,000 range while a two-year visit was funded at EUR 50,000.
Approach a host institution first. Every entry in the archive names a specific host, and a visit without a secured host is unlikely to be competitive.
Submit through the Nokia Foundation grant system, where drafts can be saved and completed later - useful because the financial and visit details often change while you negotiate.
Check the Tutkijat maailmalle page as well, since the Foundation lists it as a related call route with its own award archive and larger awards, including EUR 41,350 and EUR 36,040.
documents: The page as read publishes no required-document list. Confirm current requirements in the Nokia Foundation grant application system before submitting.
mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming a single fixed award amount. The published awards vary by more than a factor of five in a single year, so there is no standard figure to plan around.
Relying on this page for the deadline. It publishes none, and missing an unpublished deadline is the most common way a good visit application fails.
Proposing a visit with no named host. The archive shows a host organisation for every award.
Confusing this grant with the Nokia Foundation Fellow award on the same site. That one is EUR 75,000, is led by a professor, and funds hiring a researcher - a completely different instrument.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: This page publishes no deadlines at all, which is the single most important thing to know: the award archive is the content, and the call window lives elsewhere on the Nokia Foundation site. Since the most recent cohort listed is 2025, confirm with the Foundation whether a 2026 round ran before planning a visit. For context on the size of awards, the archive records EUR 20,000, EUR 25,000 and EUR 9,500 for 2025 single-year visits and EUR 50,000 for a two-year visit in 2024.
